sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match, one word or identify).

questions.q: Correct the sentences: (a) A person who sends a message is known as the receiver. (b) The receiver's response to the message is termed facts.
questions.answer:
(a) A person who sends a message is known as the sender.
(b) The receiver's response to the message is termed feedback.

questions.q: Give one-word answers: (a) Who receives the message? (b) What is exchanged in communication?
questions.answer:
(a) The receiver.
(b) Information (the message — facts, ideas, opinions).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Walking with a straight body posture shows ________. (b) ________ communication flows through officially prescribed channels.
Best answer: (a) Suman needs leave from work — which method of communication will she use? (b) Is communicating with pictures, symbols and diagrams visual communication?
questions.answer:
(a) Written communication — a leave application.
(b) Yes, it is visual communication.

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) The process of communication is complete only when the receiver understands the message. (b) The hurdle that comes in the way of communication is known as noise.
Fill in the blanks: (a) To complete the process of communication there should be at least ________ persons. (b) ________ communication includes sounds, words, language and speech.
Write True (T) or False (F): (a) Feedback is one of the elements of the communication process. (b) People in an organisation can escape from communication.
questions.answer:
(a) True
(b) False — communication is pervasive; no one can avoid it.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is video-conferencing?
questions.answer: Video-conferencing is a form of teleconferencing in which people at different places can hear and also see each other while talking, using cameras, screens and telecommunication or Internet links.

questions.q: Explain teleconferencing and audio-conferencing.
questions.answer:
Teleconferencing is a system through which people interact without physically sitting together, using telephone, computers or television.
Audio-conferencing is two-way voice communication — participants at different places hear each other and respond immediately.

questions.q: What is fax? State one advantage and one limitation.
questions.answer:
Fax (facsimile) sends an exact copy of handwritten or printed matter, diagrams and sketches instantly over telephone lines.
Advantage: instant transmission over any distance.
Limitation: only documents of a standard size; the print may fade, so copies are kept.

questions.q: State any two points of importance of communication in business.
questions.answer:
(1) It coordinates departments, controls operations and motivates employees.
(2) It links the firm with suppliers and customers and builds a good public image.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the elements of the communication process.
questions.answer:
(1) Sender — the person who starts communication and sends the message.
(2) Message — the subject matter: facts, ideas, feelings or information.
(3) Medium — the means that carries the message (letter, telephone, e-mail).
(4) Receiver — the person who receives the message.
(5) Feedback — the receiver's response directed back to the sender; it shows the message was understood.

questions.q: What is meant by filtering in communication? How does it hinder effective communication?
questions.answer:
Filtering (screening) means that when a message passes through several persons or levels, each one passes on only the part that gives a favourable impression and leaves out the rest.
It hinders communication because the message gets distorted and incomplete at each level, decisions are based on wrong information, and the top does not learn the real facts.

questions.q: Briefly explain fax and telex.
questions.answer:
Fax: an electronic device that sends an exact copy of handwritten or printed documents, diagrams and sketches instantly over telephone lines to another fax machine.
Telex: printed communication using teleprinters connected through a central exchange; a message typed on one machine is automatically typed on the other.

sections.title: Long answer questions, including case-based questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Define communication. State the various elements in the communication process.
questions.answer:
Communication is the process of sharing facts, ideas, opinions and information through speech, writing, gestures or symbols between two or more persons.
Elements: (1) Sender — the source who sends the message. (2) Message — the facts, ideas or feelings conveyed. (3) Medium — the means used (oral, written, telephone, e-mail). (4) Receiver — the person who gets the message. (5) Feedback — the receiver's response; the process is complete only when the receiver understands and responds.

questions.q: 'Communication is as necessary to business as the bloodstream is to a person.' Explain.
questions.answer:
Just as blood carries oxygen to every part of the body, communication carries information to every part of a business.
(1) It conveys plans, orders and instructions to employees.
(2) It coordinates the work of departments and helps control operations.
(3) It motivates employees and builds good relations.
(4) It links the firm with customers, suppliers and government.
(5) It helps quick decisions and builds a good public image. Without it the business cannot function.

questions.q: Explain any five barriers to effective communication.
questions.answer:
(1) Badly expressed message — poor choice of words or language causes misunderstanding.
(2) Screening or filtering — the message gets distorted as it passes through levels.
(3) Inattention — people do not read or listen carefully.
(4) Unclarified assumptions — sender and receiver assume different things.
(5) Resistance to change — people ignore messages that disturb routine.
(6) Mutual distrust; status and position; complex organisation structure.
